newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's PTT keen to buy natgas from Natuna.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's PTT keen to buy natgas from Natuna.

text.p: The state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) is keen to buy natural gas from Indonesia's mega Natuna project to meet rising domestic energy demand, PTT governor Pala Sookawesh said on Monday.
"Negotiations are ongoing. We are interested to buy from them as procurement from Natuna will ensure the stability and continuity of the supplies," he told reporters.
Thai authorities will meet Natuna representatives on May 7 in Bangkok to discuss possible purchases.

Pala said demand for natural gas will soar to 3,500 million cubic feet per day by 2000. But natural gas production in the Gulf of Thailand would peak soon and then decline making it necessary to import more.
Thailand plans to procure 2,000 mmcfd of the natural gas from indigenous sources.

The Natuna Field is one of the largest natural gas fields in the world. It contains an estimated 222 trillion cubic feet of gas, of which 46 trillion cubic feet are thought to be commercially recoverable.

The field is located in the Natuna Sea, about 225 km (135 miles) northeast of Natuna Island. Exxon has a 50 percent stake in the project and Mobil Corp 26 percent while Pertamina, Indonesia's national oil and gas company holds the rest.
